Four individuals in Mallorca have been sentenced for a significant fraud involving the sale of counterfeit olive oil. They admitted to selling low-quality and sunflower oils as extra virgin and organic, falsely labelling them as 'Oli de Mallorca' while sourcing them from mainland Spain. The Guardia Civil seized nearly 4 000 l of fraudulent oil. The defendants, including a family and a printer responsible for false labels, were convicted of industrial property crimes, forgery, and fraud. They received two-year prison sentences, fines, and were ordered to compensate affected businesses, although the prison terms were suspended.

Authorities are undertaking a comprehensive investigation to tackle the corruption and enforce stricter food safety regulations to protect public health.

In Catania, authorities have seized a large quantity of illegally caught bluefin tuna as part of efforts to combat unlawful fishing activities. The operation uncovered significant breaches of fishing regulations, leading to fines for those involved. This seizure highlights the ongoing struggle against illegal fishing practices that threaten marine ecosystems and undermine legal fishing industries. The authorities are committed to enforcing regulations to ensure sustainable fishing and the protection of marine life.

This incident highlights the need for stringent regulatory enforcement and consumer vigilance to prevent food fraud and ensure the safety of food products in the market. This deception not only misled consumers but also violated food labelling regulations. The investigation is ongoing to identify those responsible and to prevent similar occurrences in the future. This case highlights the necessity for stringent oversight and transparency in food production and labelling to protect consumers and ensure market integrity.

The incident underscores the importance of stringent food safety standards and the need for rigorous enforcement to ensure public health and safety.

The confiscated oil, which entered the country illegally, posed potential risks to consumers due to the lack of regulation and quality control. This incident highlights the ongoing challenges of tackling smuggling operations and underscores the importance of enforcing trade regulations to ensure the integrity and safety of products in the market.

This incident underscores the need for stringent regulatory oversight and the importance of ensuring that all food products are subject to thorough quality checks to protect public health.

This seizure highlights the ongoing challenges faced by regulators in combating the production and sale of fraudulent alcoholic beverages. The authorities continue to intensify efforts to enforce regulations and protect public health from the dangers posed by such illicit activities.

This incident underscores the importance of transparency and compliance with animal welfare and food labelling regulations. Authorities are taking action to address the violations and ensure that consumers are not misled about the products they purchase. May & June 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

Cinnamon: EU detects fraud and safety issues in the market A recent investigation has uncovered a significant issue with irregular cinnamon imports in Europe. Large quantities of cinnamon, allegedly originating from Asia, have been found to contain excessive levels of coumarin, a toxic substance that can pose serious health risks to consumers. The affected cinnamon, which has been distributed across several European countries, has been deemed non-compliant with EU food safety regulations. As a result, authorities have issued warnings and initiated recalls to protect public health. This incident highlights the need for stricter controls on food imports and more effective monitoring of the supply chain to prevent the entry of contaminated or adulterated products into the European market. incidents.description: In a food-factory in Diyarbakır, 2 230 kg of expired marinated chicken, minced meat, vegetables and spices — some with “2023” expiry dates — were seized and the premises shut down.
About 1 125 l of illicit liquor worth roughly EUR 2 430 were seized and four suspects arrested.
A batch of about 7 t of rice smuggled from Uzbekistan into Kyrgyzstan was seized.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: In Durango, an investigation found that around 20% of beef being sold was actually horse meat. October & November 2025 – JRC Food

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Over 7.6 t of unsafe food and 2 452 l of mineral water in unhygienic conditions were seized.
Seizure of 500 l of spurious liquor and the arrest of two militants.
Two arrested after authorities seized about 4 781 l of illicit foreign liquor.
India seized two trucks carrying paddy (rice) worth about EUR 7 800 that lacked valid documents.
Over 3 500 kg of fish without traceability were seized in eastern Sicily.

incidents.description: Authorities seized and destroyed 1 500 kg of rotten meat

categories: Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Customs in the Philippines intercepted two containers declared as carrying 5 300 cartons of fish balls but instead found bulk sacks of frozen chicken breasts.
Over 8 t of non-traceable fish with expiration dates exceeded by over a year were seized in Piombino.
A couple were arrested after being found with approximately 360 l of allegedly counterfeit olive oil. October & November 2025 – JRC Food

categories: Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Authorities seized 9 720 l of substandard oil and 2 200 kg of dead poultry.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: A coordinated police operation uncovered serious food-safety and labour violations: about EUR 50 000 in fines were issued, 350 kg of food (meat, fish, sauces, rice, prepared dishes) were seized.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Lapu-Lapu City authorities seized over 3 t of improperly stored chicken and pork, transported without valid registration and mixed in unsafe conditions.
A truck carrying 575 cartons of foreign liquor, reportedly worth EUR 82 000, was seized by police in Lucknow while being smuggled to Bihar.
Eleven people were arrested after police busted an illegal foreign-liquor production ring in Bokaro, seizing 360 l of raw spirit and 1 563 l of ready liquor.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: About 13 000 kg of pasta, meats and cheeses worth over EUR 90 000 were seized in Bologna after being stored among tires, insects and debris in unsafe conditions. The operator was fined EUR 5 000.
Authorities arrested 21 people and seized 291 t of flour and 28 t of wheat in an antismuggling operation. October & November 2025 – JRC Food
The Policía Fiscal seized more than 900 boxes of contraband whisky in Pucusana.

categories: Dietetic foods, food supplements and fortified foods
incidents.description: ANMAT banned the diabetes drug TIRZEC® 5 and 18 dietary supplements after detecting they were sold without registration or quality controls.
Nagpur police arrested seven people and seized 135 l of diluted liquor falsely sold as a major brand, worth about EUR 34 000.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: IFA destroyed 25 000 l of adulterated milk and 178 kg of unsafe meat after inspecting 1 058 restaurants and food outlets.

Valencian farmers denounce that rice brands use Valencian symbols to imply local origin without stating where the rice actually comes from, breaching EU labelling rules. A formal complaint was filed after authorities gave no response for over a month.
Bangladesh Coast Guard seized 4 000 kg of illegally traded young hilsa worth about EUR 22 500.
São Paulo authorities seized over 140 000 bottles and 500 000 fake packaging items and arrested 46 people after 47 methanol poisonings and 9 deaths linked to illicit alcohol.
Police in Goa dismantled a liquor-smuggling racket, seizing over 12 000 falsely labelled whiskey bottles worth about EUR 17 000. Four people were arrested. October & November 2025 – JRC Food
NACADA seized about 50 000 l of illicit beer and other illegal alcohol in Kericho during a dawn raid.
European fishermen warn that some sea bass sold in Spain is actually cheaper Asian perch, undermining a sector worth EUR 131 million for 23 622 t.
Turkey seized over 30 800 bottles and 21 400 l of illicit alcohol, arresting 179 people in a nationwide crackdown.
Police seized 1 238 kg of illegally harvested fish worth about EUR 4 800 in Namibia, along with banned nets.
Authorities seized 25 800 l of fake soft drinks and related materials, arresting two suspects.
Police in Bokaro seized a truck carrying 1 100 crates of illicit foreign liquor, valued at about EUR 65 000.
Liquor reportedly valued at around EUR 70 000 was seized by police in Gujarat after undercover officers intercepted a truck and car transporting 18 304 bottles hidden under groundnut sacks.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: A farm in Mormanno, Italy was raided and more than 1 100 kg of cheese, plus 96 kg of salami and 74 kg of spices, were seized after inspections found serious hygiene and labelling violations.
A police operation in Abruzzo uncovered a fraud involving “organic” honey: about 50 000 kg of honey and 12 000 kg of un-certified sugars and feed were seized. October & November 2025 – JRC Food

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: PFA seized about 45 000 kg of spoiled jam and fruit preserves stored in unsafe, unsanitary conditions. The confiscated goods were worth roughly EUR 1.5 million.
A supplier provided about 6.8 million kg of fake ghee, made from palm oil, not milk, to the TTD for making laddus, causing an estimated loss of EUR 28 million.

Police and excise officers in Andhra Pradesh destroyed 2 900 bottles of illegal liquor, removing them from circulation to prevent public harm. The bottles had been seized during enforcement actions against illicit alcohol distribution.
Sardinian authorities seized 7.5 t of untraceable seafood and issued EUR 30 000 in fines for illegal fishing and missing documentation.
Authorities seized 20 000 kg of wine worth €150 000 due to incorrect labels and missing traceability documents.
Italian authorities in Naples seized 1 500 kg of unsafe seafood: 1 200 kg of fish sold without traceability documents and 300 kg of illegally caught mussels. Fines totalled EUR 7 500.

categories: Dietetic foods, food supplements and fortified foods
incidents.description: Authorities in Nasca seized over 8 t of fake table salt in 25 kg sacks, sold with copied brand packaging and lacking proper iodine, creating a public-health risk.

categories: Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: SENASA seized 3 000 kg of chicken on Route 7 near Luján because it was being transported without required sanitary controls, proper documentation, or assurance of cold-chain conditions. October & November 2025 – JRC Food
A supplier delivered 6.8 million kg of fake ghee, made from cheap oils instead of dairy, to the Tirumala temple, worth about EUR 28 million.

Italian health-protection police shut down an illegal food warehouse operating without authorization and in very poor hygiene conditions. They seized around 1 600 eggs, 11 kg of honey and 350 l of oil, all lacking traceability. The activity was valued at about EUR 100 000, and the owner received EUR 12 500 in fines.

Portuguese authority ASAE seized over 5 t of falsified honey in Évora and Aljustrel. The honey was labelled as the operator’s own production, but it actually came from third-party producers. Packages also carried a forged veterinary-control number, misleading consumers about origin and traceability.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Authorities seized over 1 600 kg of pork in Zapala after finding it transported without refrigeration and without required sanitary documents or traceability.
Police in São Paulo and Paraná seized over 100 000 fake alcoholic drinks and arrested suspects involved in producing and selling counterfeit branded beverages.

Brazilian authorities disqualified four olive-oil brands after discovering they contained other vegetable oils instead of pure olive oil. The products were removed from the market and consumers were advised to stop using them.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Police in Sarawak seized about EUR 740 000 worth of contraband during Operation Taring. The goods included untaxed cigarettes, liquor, frozen sausages (19 200 packs), gas cylinders and rice, all smuggled without valid documentation. Several suspects were arrested for storing and distributing these illegal products.

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: ANMAT banned seven coffee products from the brands Caffé del Doge, Café Sol and Caffé del Ponte Rialto because their labels showed false or invalid sanitary-registration numbers and lacked required information such as batch and expiry dates. The products were considered fake in terms of regulatory compliance, and their sale, online and offline, was prohibited. October & November 2025 – JRC Food
Six people in Atlántida, Honduras died after drinking an adulterated local alcohol. Authorities are investigating the source and seizing remaining product.

Authorities in Sicily seized 5 550 kg of seafood unfit for consumption during Operazione Calypso. Across 990 inspections, they issued EUR 87 000 in fines, recorded 70 violations, confiscated illegal fishing gear and suspended one business due to illegal fishing practices and lack of hygiene and traceability.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Authorities in the Crotone area discovered that 13 horses, many without identification and some registered as not suitable for human consumption, were illegally slaughtered in a sealed, non-authorised facility. About 3 000 kg of horse meat and assets worth more than EUR 3 million were seized. One person was arrested and others charged for illegal slaughtering, animal cruelty, and selling unsafe food.

Authorities in Kelantan seized 40 t of white rice that was being transported without valid documentation, valued at roughly EUR 28 000. The police detained the driver and confiscated the rice and truck.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: A truck was stopped at the highway exit near Brescia carrying 1 035 kg of meat that was transported thawed rather than frozen, with storage temperature recorded at +1 °C instead of the required –18 °C. The meat was seized by authorities due to serious violations of hygiene and food-transport regulations.
A container truck near Ahmedabad was seized after police discovered about 9 476 bottles of liquor (750 ml and 180 ml) plus 4 512 beer cans hidden inside, total illicit cargo value approx. EUR 73 000.

Seven fishermen from Andhra Pradesh were arrested for fishing inside Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary, a protected zone in India, despite a ban. Authorities seized their trawler, two GPS devices, one VHF radio, a fish-finder, two generators, and about 1000 kg of fish.

A task force in Minas Gerais (Brazil) seized about 182,8 thousand l of alcoholic beverages lacking provenance or showing signs of tampering, and destroyed roughly 3 900 containers, during a 40-day operation covering 522 establishments. Eighteen people were arrested and dozens of investigations opened, while authorities carried out consumer-education actions to warn about irregular drinks.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: The producers of Prosciutto di Parma DOP were found guilty of using pigs with prohibited genetics (often heavier Danish-Duroc crossbreeds) and exceeding the allowed live-weight limit for DOP certification. This “genetic fraud” affected millions of hams meant to be sold under the DOP seal, their label and origin did not comply. A court ordered over EUR 1 million in damages to restore the reputation of the DOP and to strengthen control mechanisms. October & November 2025 – JRC Food
Authorities seized 15 000 l of adulterated milk and 3 700 kg of illegal ingredients at an unlicensed facility.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: More than 27 000 boxes of canned goods, allegedly containing horse meat instead of the declared meat, were seized by prosecutors and police across 13 sites linked to the Qali Warma school-feeding program. Three people were arrested, including a former program official, while authorities announced efforts to capture additional suspects connected to the distribution of adulterated food to children.

In Palma authorities seized 20 t of expired and refrozen seafood from a distributor, including batches whose best-before dates go back to 2019. The firm was fined EUR 90 000 for serious breaches of food-safety and storage regulations.
Authorities in Ukraine dismantled a criminal network producing fake food, including canned goods and condensed milk, mimicking well-known brands, seizing nearly EUR 460 000 worth of goods.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: A meat-processing plant in Budapest was shut down after inspectors found mouldy meat on the walls and dead insects on the floor, the facility’s hygiene conditions were described as “shocking.” The closure came amid fears of potential foodborne illness, and authorities removed all affected meat from circulation.

Seized over 42 000 kg of tomato puree transported from Bulgaria were seized at the port of Brindisi while they were falsely labeled as “Made in Italy”, destined for two Italian firms. The producers’ documents declared a Bulgarian origin, but the cans bore labels claiming Italian origin, misleading consumers.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: During the operation Adegas do Crime in Formiga, authorities seized liquor (cachaça), cheese, and salami due to suspected adulteration and sanitary irregularities. The crackdown targeted illegal alcohol falsification and prevented unfit, potentially dangerous products from reaching the market.

Authorities in Himachal Pradesh Excise Department seized 54 945 l of illegal liquor across the state in a wide crackdown, disrupting several illicit distilleries. Special enforcement teams carried out multiple raids, registered hundreds of cases, and destroyed unauthorized production units on the spot.

Authorities intercepted a cargo of 564 bottles of wine deemed contraband on a road between Sucre Department and Bolívar Department. The merchandise was valued at EUR 6 500. The wine lacked proper documentation proving its legality and origin, which led to its seizure. October & November 2025 – JRC Food

A gang was busted in Hazaribag district, after police seized illicit foreign liquor valued at about EUR 76 000. Authorities confiscated 332 cartons, a total of 15 936 bottles, plus materials used to produce counterfeit liquor, four vehicles and several phones.
The government of Indonesia seized about 250 t of rice from a warehouse in Sabang Free Trade Zone, Aceh, after discovering it had been imported illegally from Thailand without proper authorization.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: A recent inspection by law-enforcement and customs agents at a meat-processing facility in Piacenza led to the seizure of about 2 000 kg of meat. The owner was fined EUR 25 500 and the irregular meat was confiscated. The seized products lacked proper stamping/marking and traceability, meaning they could not be certified as safe or compliant.
A food-authority raid in Rawalpindi dismantled a network producing 15 000 l of adulterated milk made with dry powder and salt.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: A meat-processing company in Mantua reportedly thawed and re-processed expired meat, from South America, New Zealand and Eastern Europe, then re-packaged it with new expiry dates and put it back on the market. The repackaged meat was allegedly distributed to restaurants, supermarkets and possibly pet-food channels, prompting a food-safety alert and seizure orders from health authorities.

A large operation by the coast guard in Veneto led to the seizure of 42 t of octopus imported from Vietnam and India, originally labeled as Octopus membranaceus but actually belonging to different species. The octopuses had incorrect or misleading labeling.

During a coordinated raid near the wholesale market in Budapest, authorities seized about 6 000 kg of walnuts, 2 500 kg of grapes and several additional hundred kilograms of other vegetables and fruits whose origin could not be documented. The vendors, mostly Romanian nationals using trucks with hidden compartments, had no valid traceability or paperwork for the produce. Fines imposed by the customs authority may exceed EUR 22 000, and a foodsafety investigation has been launched due to lack of proper marking and traceability.

categories: Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: About 25 000 kg of expired chicken products, including döner, liver, tripe and sausage, were seized in an inspection in the Aksu district of Antalya. The items had passed their expiration date and had been repackaged for sale; all were confiscated and destroyed.

Former minister Jogi Ramesh was arrested after a major investigation uncovered that a network was producing and distributing fake liquor in his home state. Authorities found over 10 000 l of adulterated alcohol, and accused him of financing and directing the operation, with a suspected money trail of around EUR 330 000. October & November 2025 – JRC Food

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: About 14 880 single-dose tea bags labelled as “slimming teas” from brands Meridetox Tea Premium and Ozlex Tea, imported from Turkey, were seized by customs and financial police in the port of Trieste. Laboratory analysis found undeclared Sibutramina, a banned weight-loss drug, inside the tea.

A police operation at Mercasevilla in Seville confiscated over 1 000 kg of seafood, including tuna, hake, sole and red mullet, because the products lacked the legally required traceability documentation and some fish were under-size for sale.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: During a roadside inspection in Hatay, authorities seized 1 t of meat lacking any veterinary health certificate and with unknown origin.
The Uganda Revenue Authorityt seized 10 t of wheat flour smuggled from Kenya hidden in a Fuso truck at the border.

Police in Medellín seized 17 296 empty bottles that were cleaned and ready to be refilled with allegedly adulterated whisky and tequila. Also confiscated were some 8 000 brand-logo stickers, 10 000 original caps, 300 fabric bags and 5 000 original boxes, materials intended to falsify legitimate liquor. This operation prevented hundreds or thousands of litres of dangerous alcohol (potentially containing toxic contaminants) from reaching consumers. October & November 2025 – JRC Food

In December 2025, Colombian authorities seized contraband and counterfeit goods worth EUR 1.7 million during "Plan Navidad" operations. The seizures included thousands of units of mislabelled or adulterated liquor and various food products lacking sanitary records.

Authorities in Bogotá dismantled a distribution center for counterfeit alcohol, seizing more than 4 000 bottles and boxes of various spirits (whiskey, rum, vodka, and champagne) valued at approximately EUR 92 500.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Italian authorities seized 180 t of expired meat. The company allegedly altered expiration dates and health certificates to resell unfit food.

Italian authorities in Naples seized 11 000 bottles of Campari and Cinzano. The operation resulted in the confiscation of illicit goods, which were intended for the holiday market. Investigators found that the products lacked proper traceability and featured forged excise stamps. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

Police in Jamtara seized a massive consignment of spurious liquor worth approximately EUR 41 000 intended for Bihar. The operation resulted in the confiscation of 5 400 bottles, along with 78 gallons (3 120 l) of spirit concealed in bags of snacks inside a truck. Four alleged smugglers were arrested during the operation.

During a national inspection of 350 buffets and restaurants in Hungary, authorities confiscated 1 300 kg of non-compliant food products and imposed total fines of approximately EUR 44 700. The operation resulted in 85 legal procedures and the immediate closure of 25 units due to severe traceability and safety issues.

categories: Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Police in Treinta y Tres seized over 3 t of smuggled chicken breasts being transported in a truck without proper refrigeration. The Brazilian-origin poultry was entering Uruguay illegally to avoid customs and health controls..

Authorities in Quito dismantled a criminal network, seizing approximately 10 000 bottles of adulterated liquor and 2 000 l of artisanal alcohol. The counterfeit goods included forged labels of recognized brands and 10 000 dispensers.

Ahmedabad police seized 53 369 bottles of illicit liquor from a truck on the SP Ring Road. The seized alcohol is valued at approximately EUR 110 000, and the operation is classified as Grey Market as the cargo was hidden under animal hair to evade prohibition laws...

Cypriot authorities seized over 1 000 bottles of counterfeit vodka in a coordinated operation at four premises Nicosia. According to the authorities, a search of the premises revealed a total of 434 bottles of 1 l each and 568 bottles of 0.7 l, infringing the property rights of a wellknown brand of alcoholic beverages.

Authorities in Barranquilla dismantled a clandestine factory. In the warehouse, which had no business name and was hidden among residential properties, the officers found two alcohol storage tanks with a capacity of 10 000 millilitres each, a bottling machine, more than 7 000 bottles ready to be filled and another 2 000 in the process, as well as 20 000 caps, 1 000 stamps and 2 000 counterfeit security seals.

ASAE seized 2 425 l of adulterated oil and 1 217 counterfeit labels during the operation in Porto. This food fraud involved a product consisting of vegetable oil flavored with dyes to mimic authentic olive oil. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud
Indian-Made Foreign Liquor worth nearly EUR 160 600 was seized in separate raids in Mundra and Aravalli districts, indicating illegal import and distribution activities.

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: Authorities in Biankouma, arrested 4 fraudulent cocoa buyers for engaging in Misdescription/Mislabelling and Document forgery by attempting to bypass official pricing and trade regulations.

South African police dismantled an illegal alcohol production plant in Lansdowne and confiscated counterfeit goods, including alcohol with fake brand labels. Two suspects were arrested for manufacturing and distributing illegal alcohol.

Turkish authorities conducted a massive nationwide operation against counterfeit alcohol, seizing 119 564 bottles of illicit liquids. The confiscated goods included 48 425 l of ethyl alcohol and 2 792 l of illegal beverages. This coordinated raid across 81 provinces led to the detention of 169 suspects and the dismantling of 12 illegal production sites.

The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force confiscated 13 812 bottles of illicit liquor, hidden beneath sacks of potatoes in a truck. This smuggling operation, intended for distribution in Bihar, resulted in the arrest of one individual and the seizure of the vehicle and a mobile phone.

Italian authorities seized 2 800 kg of clams in Goro (Ferrara), issuing fines totaling EUR 27 000. This food fraud case involved mollusks transported without proper documentation, preventing their legal entry into the market.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Hungarian authorities seized 4 t of processed meat products during a roadside inspection in Röszke. The shipment lacked required traceability documents and proper temperature control.

Authorities in Sonbhadra confiscated 5 960 265 l of illicit Punjab-made liquor, comprising 15 669 bottles, after a truck overturned. The seized shipment, valued at approximately EUR 47 000, was concealed under sacks of rice to evade taxes during transit to Jharkhand. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

The Malaysian Border Agency confiscated non-compliant food products at the Bukit Kayu Hitam border, valued at approximately EUR 13 500. The seizure included vegetables lacking mandatory certification and seafood (vannamei prawns, giant freshwater prawns, fish, and oyster meat) that exceeded declared amounts.

Authorities in northern Morocco seized over 6 500 l of adulterated olive oil, targeting fraudulent practices in production areas. The seized oils were found to be non-authentic mixtures sold to unsuspecting consumers.

Authorities uncovered a Grey Market fraud where thousands of tons of Anna Bhagya subsidy rice were illegally diverted for export to Dubai and Singapore. Police confiscated approximately 3 000 t of food supplies during raids in December 2025.

Police in Ahmedabad confiscated 7 108 bottles of illicit liquor hidden inside 1 144 boxes of Bournvita chocolate drink. The seized alcohol, including 750 ml and 180 ml whisky and rum bottles, was valued at approximately EUR 41 000. Authorities also seized a container truck, a car, and a motorcycle, bringing the total value of confiscated assets to nearly EUR 146 000.

The excise department in Gaya confiscated approximately 13 320 bottles of illicit foreign liquor, with an estimated market value of EUR 37 000. The product was seized during regular raids on a truck and in Mufassil. The operation resulted in the arrest of the truck driver and the confiscation of 320 cartons used to conceal the illegal shipment.

A 75-year-old woman and four relatives were arrested in South Africa for allegedly selling rotten and expired food for human consumption. The suspects are accused of repackaging decomposed food and distributing it illegally. Authorities discovered large quantities of unsafe food stored on a farm, along with related equipment and vehicles.

Police seized 15 552 bottles of illicit liquor worth approximately EUR 190 000 hidden inside a cement bulker truck. The 1 296 confiscated cartons were being smuggled into Ahmedabad for New Year celebrations. The total seizure, including the vehicle and assets, is valued at EUR 216 000, measured by a transport capacity of one heavy-duty truck.

Authorities in Antalya, Turkey uncovered a food fraud operation in which expired products were being relabelled with new expiration dates to make them appear safe for sale. The scheme was discovered during an inspection by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry. Officials found equipment used to print and replace labels, confirming deliberate consumer deception. All affected products were seized and destroyed to protect public health. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

Police in Kwekwe intercepted a truck and confiscated 13.96 T of food products. The operation involved 698 bags (20 kg each) of fake Huletts sugar. The seized goods, valued at approximately EUR 12 400, were being delivered to a local wholesale outlet without authorization. Four suspects were arrested for violating the Trade Marks Act following verification by the brand's loss control officers.

Moroccan customs authorities dismantled a large network of illegal warehouses used to store smuggled and counterfeit goods across several regions. The operation uncovered clandestine depots hidden as farms and stables, run by organized fraud networks using shell companies. Investigators identified major customs and tax fraud through falsified import documents and international data analysis. Seized goods included adulterated alcohol and spoiled spices.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Turkish authorities confiscated exactly 1.9 t of beef that was being transported illegally in an unrefrigerated vehicle in the Efeler district. The meat lacked health stamps, origin documentation, and proper thermal control. The illicit shipment was destroyed by officials to prevent it from entering the local market.

Burkina Faso's National Coordination for the Fight against Fraud seized over 30 t of rice that was being illegally repackaged. The operation targeted a warehouse where low-quality or expired rice was transferred into high-end brand bags.

Colombian authorities upheld sanctions against four dairy companies after detecting the illegal addition of lactoserum to milk. The investigation involved the analysis of thousands of liters of product, resulting in fines totaling approximately EUR 2.7 million.

Authorities seized various quantities including 12 bottles of Haryana-sourced spirits and 1 100 l of illicit wash. The operation targeted illegal transport and sale, resulting in the dismantling of three distilleries and the arrest of multiple individuals.

The Genoa Coast Guard seized 6 t of expired and untraceable seafood (cephalopods) during an inspection in Milan. The operation resulted in fines totaling EUR 3 500 for serious violations regarding food safety and storage.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: The Portuguese Food and Economic Safety Authority seized 563 kg of frozen meat from a meat processing operator in Faro after inspections found serious irregularities in traceability, freezing and packaging practices that violated food-safety laws. The meat was judged abnormal and potentially unsafe, triggering both criminal and administrative actions against the operator. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

The Turkish Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry added 36 new products to its official food blacklist of counterfeit or adulterated items that pose health risks, including olive oil, yogurt and honey. Recent tests found misleading labelling and contamination issues, such as starch in “plain” yogurt and mixed seed oils in supposed olive oil.
Authorities in Valledupar seized over 3 000 bottles of illicit liquor at the Mercabastos market. The products lacked legal tax stamps and health registrations required for sale.

Authorities in Gurugram conducted a major raid at "The Theka Wine Shop," seizing approximately 40 000 bottles (3 900 cases) of illicit foreign liquor worth EUR 1.1 million. The products lacked valid holograms and were smuggled illegally into a licensed outlet to evade taxes. All units were confiscated during the evening operation after complaints revealed the sale of untracked goods. This seizure represents the largest ever recorded at a single high-end liquor vend in the state.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Italian authorities conducted a major raid in Rome's Esquilino district, seizing 1.5 t of irregular food products, including meat and fish. The operation resulted in fines of EUR 50 000, as the products lacked traceability and the appropriate health certifications. All non-compliant food items were confiscated and destroyed during the inspection to ensure public safety.

The Punjab Food Authority recently sealed a production unit, confiscating and destroying 36 000 kg of hazardous marmalade and fruit preserves.The facility used textile dyes, artificial sweeteners, and rotten fruit without proper labelling.

The State Excise Department confiscated an illegal shipment of Indian-made foreign liquor valued at approximately EUR 46 900. The vehicle was carrying several hundred kilograms of illicit alcohol, specifically 1 000 cartons of liquor and beer, which were seized immediately after the accident.

Customs officials in Tenkodogo seized a major shipment of smuggled liquor concealed within a large transport vehicle. The operation resulted in the confiscation of 363 cartons of smuggled alcoholic beverages, including vodka, whisky, scotch, sangria and other spirits, intended for illicit distribution during the year-end festive season. The products lacked the mandatory tax stamps and legal documentation required for the region. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

The Navi Mumbai Excise Department seized 1 550 boxes of illicit Indian-made foreign liquor worth approximately EUR 170 000. Goa-manufactured alcohol was being smuggled into Maharashtra to evade taxes and bypass local bans. While no specific food quantities were confiscated other than the alcoholic beverages, the entire shipment was intercepted during a special drive for the Christmas and New Year season.

The Ahmedabad Police Control Branch confiscated 15 996 bottles of illicit Indian Made Foreign Liquor valued at approximately EUR 72 600. The illegal shipment was smuggled and concealed beneath cartons of fresh oranges to evade prohibition laws.

The Guardia di Finanza in Termoli seized approximately 1.5 t of illegally caught fish and 300 kg of fish lacking proper documentation. The operation involved several commercial activities where officers confiscated the fish to protect public health. The administrative fines imposed on the offenders totaled exceed EUR 200 000, as the products were deemed unsafe due to the lack of information regarding their origin and processing.

The Islamabad Food Authority dismantled a massive production unit in Khanna Syedan that was manufacturing 100 000 l of synthetic milk daily. The criminal operation involved mixing powder, water, and vegetable ghee to sell a hazardous liquid as pure milk. Authorities confiscated and destroyed 50 000 liters of prepared fake milk, along with 105 bags of powder and 250 tins of oil.

South Africa’s agriculture minister confirmed that fake or adulterated honey has been found mainly in informal, non-franchise outlets, not major supermarkets, raising consumer and industry concerns; inspectors seized 1 059 honey-like syrups and 388 mislabelled products. These fake products are often diluted with cheaper sweeteners, misleading buyers and depressing prices for real beekeepers.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Authorities in northern Italy seized thousands of kilograms of beef linked to suspected food fraud after a TV inquiry showed expired frozen meat being thawed, relabelled and redistributed. About 1 500 kg destined for cruise ship catering were pulled from the market, 100 kg delivered to a restaurant were already consumed, and 3 000 kg sent to a pet food producer had also been used, prompting health officials to block and confiscate additional lots while investigations continue.

The Punjab Food Authority and IFA dismantled a major counterfeit and aulteration network near Faizabad. During the raid, officials confiscated and destroyed approximately 27 000 l of fake milk, along with 3 200 kg of ghee and 2 500 kg of dry milk powder. This illicit operation involved the illegal mixing of powder and vegetable oil to mimic real dairy.

In a joint intelligence-based operation, Pakistan Rangers Sindh and Customs enforcement seized a large consignment of smuggled goods hidden in warehouses near Yousuf Goth and Hub River Road. The confiscated food items included significant quantities of dry milk, Iranian toffees and chocolates, Chinese salt, dairy milk cream, and other assorted food items, transported in 10 trucks. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

The Guardia di Finanza in Fasano (Brindisi) dismantled a food fraud operation involving the seizure of 391 l of product. The primary fraud type was Adulteration, as laboratory tests revealed a mixture of olive and seed oils sold as "100% Italian extra virgin olive oil," along with Misbranding due to labels lacking mandatory traceability information.

The Uganda Revenue Authority intercepted a truck along the Tororo-Jinja highway carrying 3.2 t of smuggled Kenyan rice. The contraband was strategically hidden beneath a consignment of cement bags to evade detection and tax obligations.

The Kalyan Excise Vigilance team intercepted a container on the Mumbai-Nashik highway, seizing illicit liquor worth approximately EUR 93 600. The alcohol was found hidden behind a consignment of Maggi noodles inside a large vehicle used as cover to evade taxes. Authorities confiscated the entire illegal shipment, which was being smuggled from Goa and Madhya Pradesh for New Year celebrations.
Police in Jharkhand seized 25 440 bottles of illegal foreign liquor worth about EUR 110 000 being smuggled from Uttar Pradesh to Bihar, resulting in the driver's arrest.

Jorhat police seized 20 000 l of illicit country liquor 'Sulai' and destroyed 10 distillation units in a crackdown on illegal liquor trade. The operation targeted the production infrastructure and confiscated raw materials used in bootleg liquor production. 'Sulai' is often adulterated with toxic substances, posing a deadly threat to economically vulnerable workers.

Trinidad and Tobago police dismantled a major smuggling ring, seizing illicit alcohol and cigarettes from Suriname valued at approximately EUR 1.25 million. The products lacked legal import permits and tax documentation.
Turkish authorities detained 66 suspects and seized large quantities of counterfeit and smuggled alcohol in nationwide raids, uncovering illegal production facilities.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: The Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group seized EUR 1.43 million worth of frozen food without permits in Navotas City, potentially involving illegal smuggling and posing safety risks. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud
40 t of smuggled wheat were seized, indicating unauthorized sales channels.

Authorities uncovered a collection of 900 bottles of exclusive French and Italian wine smuggled into Albania valued at EUR 1 000 000. The goods were illegally imported to evade EUR 300 000 in customs duties. But the wine collection disappeared in an unprecedented manner, after it was blocked by Bureau of Investigation officers and the Customs Investigation Directorate. Currently, no physical quantities remain confiscated as the product "disappeared without a trace" from the owner's villa.
The Punjab Food Authority in Multan disposed of 222 000 l of adulterated milk and 40 000 rotten eggs as part of their enforcement operations against food fraud.

In 2025, Brazil’s Anvisa and the Ministry of Agriculture banned 25 olive oil brands, as lab tests revealed the illegal presence of other vegetable oils. The article highlights the extensive list of prohibited brands and the reasons for the ban on oils.

Colombian authorities seized over 10 000 bottles in 2025 of illicit liquor and identified 56 000 additional units in official warehouses. The fraud involves hazardous substances like methanol and forged tax stamps.

Authorities at Linate Airport seized 6.5 t of dangerous food products, including animal and plant-based products. The confiscated goods were smuggled in by passengers from various countries, posing a risk of introducing infectious diseases.
Malaysian authorities seized 41 t of smuggled rice valued at approximately EUR 298 000 near the northern border. The products bypassed official trade channels and lacked proper documentation.

The Delhi Crime Branch dismantled a major food fraud syndicate involved in Product Tampering and Mislabelling of expired international goods. Authorities confiscated a massive shipment of branded food and baby formula valued at approximately EUR 400 000, which was being illegally repackaged with fake barcodes and forged expiry dates. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

During the "Fish Net" operation conducted in December 2025, the Italian Coast Guard seized approximately 130 t of seafood products across the national territory. The operation involved lack of traceability and expired products intended for holiday consumption.
In December 2025, Bari authorities seized 5 000 kg of frozen fish lacking mandatory traceability. The confiscated seafood, intended for Christmas consumption.

A parallel black market for fish products was discovered in Italy, involving illegal fishing beyond quotas and selling without traceability or proper documentation. Police confiscated approximately 3 800 kg of clams, 700 kg of fish products and imposed fines totaling EUR 28 000 against the offenders.

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: 10 900 kg of stolen coffee products valued at over EUR 83 000 were seized at a warehouse in Melrose Park.

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: Delhi Police busted a massive food fraud racket seizing 43 762 kg of expired food products. The confiscated stock included 14 665 l of beverages, 6 047 kg of snacks, biscuits, wafers, candies and chocolates, and 23 050 kg of sauces, all recovered at multiple locations in Pahari Dheeraj and Faiz Ganj in Delhi’s Sadar Bazar.

A large consignment of Indian-made foreign liquor was seized from a warehouse in Ahmedabad, as part of a crackdown against illegal liquor sales. The consignment included 1 152 liquor bottles valued at EUR 13 600, and three individuals were arrested under the Gujarat Prohibition Act.

Over 85 000 packages of instant noodles were seized at the port of Genova-Prà destined for the italian market. The shipment was seized after lab tests confirmed the presence of unauthorized animal proteins that were intentionally omitted from the Italian labels to bypass health controls, violating EU food safety regulations.
Cofepris issued an alert regarding three falsified batches of baby milk formula, posing health risks due to non-compliance with sanitary regulations. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud
A major raid in Muğla, Türkiye, led to the seizure of 1 t of counterfeit alcohol before it could be released into the market. The operation resulted in the detention of 5 suspects.

Border Police in Costa Rica seized 10 000 units of smuggled alcohol due to tax evasion and lack of invoices. The confiscation included 8 664 units of beer, 960 units of flavored vodka/spirits, 408 units of rum with cola, and 32 l of pure rum. The illegal merchandise was intercepted in a truck in the La Gamba sector, Guaycará de Golfito.

Federal authorities in Puerto Iguazú dismantled a major food fraud operation of olive oil, where illegal shipments worth approximately EUR 420 000 per week were moved. The oils had been marketed under the brand name ‘Viejo Olivar’, although packaging, labels and presentations from brands widely recognised in the domestic market, such as 'Molinos Río de la Plata' and 'Cocinero', had also been used. These adulterated oils, which were deemed unfit for human consumption, were being distributed to local restaurants and food shops. The investigation continues with one suspect in custody.

Dahod police seized Indian Made Foreign Liquor worth EUR 146 000 from a village near the Gujarat-Madhya Pradesh border. More than 25 000 bottles of liquor were recovered from a truck, indicating illegal transport and trade.
The Kondhwa police in Pune seized over EUR 173 920 and liquor worth EUR 1 930 during a raid on an illicit liquor den, indicating illegal trade and smuggling of alcoholic beverages.

Bodegas in Sevilla are accused of selling wines falsely labelled with Denomination of Origin Protections and Indication Geographical Protections from Condado de Huelva, exploiting the prestige of these labels without meeting legal requirements.

Authorities confirmed the seizure of over 600 units of expired food products. A business owner in Bahrain was jailed and fined approximately EUR 230 000. The criminal operation involved Product tampering by removing original expiry dates and replacing them with forged labels to extend shelf life illegally.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Authorities uncovered a case involving expired gyros meat. In December, the National Food Chain Safety Office confiscated 1.3 t of meat products that lacked traceability or had their expiry dates manipulated. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: Authorities seized 828 units of expired food products, including candies, cookies, coffee and panettones, from 10 food shops in Iñaquito. The expiration dates were altered to resell hazardous goods.
A wholesaler in Sestri Levante was fined EUR 32 000 for selling expired and untraceable fish products. Authorities seized 130 t of products.

categories: Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: The Punjab Food Authority discarded 5 500 litres of milk and 640 kg of diseased poultry in Lahore. The seizure involved milk contaminated with powders and chemicals to increase volume, alongside unfit meat.
Food safety authorities in Dera Ismail Khan seized 1 100 l of expired non-alcoholic beverages during a market inspection.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Armenian authorities intercepted an illegal attempt to sell 965 kg of horse meat lacking proper documentation. The food safety regulator confiscated and destroyed the entire shipment, which was intended for markets in Yerevan and Vanadzor, to prevent the sale of products of unknown origin.
Customs officers at the Kapitan Andreevo checkpoint seized 40 t of smuggled vegetables from three trucks entering from Turkey. The goods were not declared in the transit documents.

An underground workshop in Bishkek was discovered producing counterfeit vodka, involving illegal production and questionable excise stamps. Officers confiscated 110 l of artisanal alcohol, 122 units of counterfeit alcoholic products, and 2 180 forged excise stamps. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: The Bolivian Navy seized illicit pork valued at approximately EUR 54 000 during an operation at Lake Titicaca. Authorities confiscated 128 slaughtered pigs and 60 live pigs found in two abandoned vessels without legal documentation, preventing their smuggling into Peru.

categories: Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: The KP Food Authority confiscated 2 300 kg of banned Chinese salt and unsafe meat during operations in Peshawar and Nowshera. The seized items were discarded on the spot and premises were sealed.

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: A court in Ukraine ordered the destruction of hundreds of kilograms of counterfeit Lavazza coffee produced and sold under the guise of well-known brands. The operation involved largescale production and sale through various channels, leading to legal actions against the perpetrators.

categories: Dietetic foods, food supplements and fortified foods
incidents.description: Vietnam police dismantled a major smuggling ring that illegally imported nearly 50 000 units of health supplements from Canada. Authorities confiscated an entire container of supplements valued at EUR 1.5 million, including Hydro Whey Zero products in chocolate, vanilla and strawberry flavours under the Biotech brand. The crackdown, part of a security operation for the 2026 Lunar New Year, resulted in criminal proceedings against three individuals for smuggling. December 2025 – JRC Food Fraud

Mumbai police busted a milk adulteration racket in Andheri West after a food safety tip-off, arresting seven people for taking branded milk packets, diluting the contents with water and resealing them unhygienically for sale. Authorities charged the suspects under Indian law to protect consumer health and food standards.

In a January 2026 police operation in İzmir, Turkey, authorities seized about 3.5 t of ethyl alcohol and around 600 bottles of fake liquor and arrested 35 suspects linked to the production of counterfeit alcoholic drinks. The crackdown is part of ongoing efforts to combat dangerous bootleg alcohol, which has previously been tied to dozens of deaths and public health warnings in the country.

Mexican health authority has issued a health alert about counterfeit Similac baby milk formula batches being sold irregularly online and in informal markets, which may lack proper nutritional quality and safety and pose serious health risks to infants. The agency urged parents not to buy these products and to verify batch numbers against official lists to avoid unsafe ones.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: During 2025, Argentine authorities seized 17 000 kg of meat in poor condition during inspections targeting illicit slaughter and unsafe distribution, removing contaminated food from the market to protect public health. The action reflects food fraud concerns with all unsafe products prevented from entering commerce.

In Alcoholic beverages, authorities seized 1 276 bottles of expired liquor and ethyl alcohol ready for illegal sale in Bosa, Colombia, leading to two arrests and a business closure. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

Police in Andhra Pradesh destroyed 3 200 l of illicit fermented jaggery wash, a key ingredient for illegal liquor, during anti-bootlegging raids in Narsipatnam, aiming to curb unlicensed distillation and distribution. The operation was part of broader efforts to crack down on illicit alcohol production in the region.
Six people were arrested in Nadawa, for allegedly selling alcoholic beverages without a valid license after police seized assorted products during a raid.

The Regional Tax Office-II in Karachi detained three trucks carrying 1 800 sugar bags with fake Track & Trace System stamps during an enforcement operation at Sassi Toll Plaza, aiming to curb tax evasion and illegal movement of essential goods. The trucks, allegedly loaded from Chambar Sugar Mills, were moved to RTO-II’s NIPA premises for investigation and legal action under applicable laws.

Police in Rajasthan seized illegal liquor worth about EUR 140 300 from a truck on the DelhiMumbai Expressway in Dausa, hiding 1 071 cartons beneath rice bags. The operation by the Anti-Gang Task Force led to the arrest of a suspect and recovery of cash, with the vehicle impounded. Preliminary probes suggest the smuggled alcohol was being moved from Haryana to Gujarat.

In Bangladesh, authorities uncovered an illegal milk-production facility in Pabna, seizing large quantities of counterfeit milk and arresting the owner, who received 1 year imprisonment and a EUR 1 400 fine.

Officials from the Food Safety Department in Jammu and Kashmir conducted surprise raids in the Qamarwari and Barthana areas of Srinagar, seizing about 36 kg of adulterated ghee and 15 kg of fake honey falsely marketed as local products. The items were confiscated for laboratory analysis, and authorities are investigating the case under food safety laws to protect public health.
Indonesian authorities seized nearly 100 t of smuggled frozen Pacific mackerel at Tanjung Priok Port in Jakarta, thwarting illegal imports and protecting local fisheries markets.

Despite Indonesia restricting official peanut imports from India, large volumes of Indian peanuts continue entering Indonesia through illegal channels, often rerouted via Malaysia’s Port Klang. Indonesian authorities are stepping up enforcement and seizures to curb these unauthorised shipments, amid stricter quality and aflatoxin requirements that have reduced legitimate trade.

Italian Guardia Costiera seized nearly 28 t of illegal and expired fish during inspections in Sassari and Nuoro. Over 26 t lacked proper traceability or were expired, posing food safety risks. Administrative fines totaling EUR 5 000 were imposed, along with the seizure of the products. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: The Punjab Food Authority inspected over 1 475 milk points and 346 meat shops, shutting two units selling unsafe milk and meat and registering two cases. They destroyed 7 516 kg of substandard meat and 345 l of harmful counterfeit milk to protect public health. Fines about EUR 8 000 were imposed on 96 food points for violations.

In Cauca, authorities dismantled a criminal network that illegally manufactured and distributed adulterated alcoholic beverages without sanitary controls, seizing more than 5 000 bottles and EUR 37 000 during raids that led to six arrests.

The Maharashtra State Excise Department in Nagpur raided an illegal factory making counterfeit Indian-made foreign liquor, seizing liquor and production materials valued at around EUR 23 000. Officials confiscated about 1 090 l of fake blend, 356 banned bottles, 90 l of another fake liquor, sealing equipment, labels, caps, bottles, and a vehicle.

Morocco’s food safety authority seized and destroyed 9 t of non-compliant olive oil and referred 58 fraud cases to justice as inspectors cracked down on sellers mislabeling lowergrade oil as virgin olive oil.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: In Polatlı, authorities seized 11 400 kg of counterfeit meat and assorted fake food products and 20 000 fraudulent labels during a smuggling-prevention operation. The items (including oils and food coloring) have an estimated market value of about EUR 187 000. Legal proceedings were launched against three suspects.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Police in Campo Grande, seized and destroyed about 2 200 kg of beef, pork, and chicken meat that was stored and handled unsafely and lacked traceability, posing public health risks. The products unfit for consumption were removed from a supermarket supply chain. The operator was charged under consumer protection law.
Police in Dahod, Gujarat seized 33 066 bottles of Indian-made foreign liquor hidden behind bubble wrap on a truck and arrested two men, with the haul valued at about EUR 127 000.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: The Indian food safety authority seized and destroyed more than 1 600 kg of contaminated pickles in Rajasthan after tests found them unsafe for consumption, alongside additional adulterated ghee and jaggery. The crackdown, part of a wider national food-safety drive, aims to protect consumers from harmful chemicals in store-bought jars. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Malaysia’s Border Control and Protection Agency seized 1.2 t of frozen beef and mutton worth over EUR 28 800 at Kuala Lumpur International Airport because the shipment from Australia lacked valid import permits and health certification, and authorities have detained the goods for further legal action.

A Sri Lankan court ordered the destruction of 2 447 cans of substandard canned fish seized in a December 2025 raid for lacking proper labels and certification. The business owner pleaded guilty and was fined about EURO 185. The fish were destroyed under court supervision at the Avissawella Magistrate’s Court.
A large-scale fraud ring illegally transformed about 3 458 700 l of wine by re-labelling cheap Spanish wine as Bordeaux and prestigious French denominations, making about EURO 1.24 million profit..

The Delhi Police dismantled an illegal liquor-mixing unit producing fake high-end branded spirits and arrested one person, seizing 173 bottles of illicit premium liquor and fake labels/stickers. The raid was part of a broader crackdown on illicit liquor production linked to health and fraud risks.

Police in Mlolongo, seized more than 2 560 bottles of suspected counterfeit liquor during a raid targeting illicit alcohol along the Nairobi–Mombasa Highway. The bottles were packed in 64 cartons and believed to be fake, though no arrests were made. Authorities are pursuing suspects.

The Malaysian agriculture ministry’s enforcement arm seized 9 750 kg of smuggled Thai white rice during a raid on a wholesaler in Selangor, following intelligence of illegal distribution. Officials also confiscated trading documents to aid the investigation. If convicted, the wholesaler faces fines of up to EUR 10 700.

The Punjab Food Authority in Multan seized 3 000 kg of adulterated spices, including fake chilli powder, turmeric, harmful chemical powder and industrial colour, from a grinding unit supplying substandard products across South Punjab.

In central Gujarat, police seized Indian-Made Foreign Liquor shipments worth about EUR 188 000 from trucks and industrial areas during coordinated operations, intercepting major consignments on highways and at industrial estates. Three people were arrested and investigations continue to track suppliers and organizers. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

In Uttar Pradesh, a court in Aligarh convicted a smuggler for supplying methanol-contaminated liquor that caused the deaths of 106 people in the 2021 adulterated alcohol tragedy, and set the sentence for 20 January 2026. The sentence was 10 years in prison and a fine of EUR 600.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: In 2025, the Carabinieri food safety unit in Padua seized around 100 t of unsafe food, including meat, dairy and bakery products lacking traceability or proper storage. Authorities carried out about 1 900 inspections, issued 757 administrative fines totaling roughly EUR 900 000, proposed closures for 23 businesses, and saw 15 people criminally charged for offences such as fraud and selling spoiled food.

Police in Varanasi arrested a suspected liquor smuggler and seized 9 000 l of illegal Indianmade foreign liquor worth about EUR 70 100 in Ballia district, with the haul hidden in a truck and the accused booked under the Excise Act.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: In 2025, Italian health police seized about 12 t of unsafe food during inspections across northern provinces, leading to temporary closures of 50 food businesses (24 in the Brescia area), 14 criminal charges, and fines totaling EUR 800 000 for hygiene and traceability violations.

In 2025, the Carabinieri NAS of Cremona carried out extensive food safety controls in the Mantua area, leading to the suspension or closure of around 24 businesses. Authorities seized about 383 t of foodstuffs worth EUR 100 million and imposed 673 administrative fines totaling over EUR 1 million.The operations also resulted in 18 criminal charges, with 54 individuals reported to judicial authorities.

In Colombia, customs authorities seized illegally imported goods valued at over EUR 250 000, including 23 000 kg of tilapia lacking legal paperwork. The confiscated foods posed potential safety hazards due to missing sanitary registration.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: The Carabinieri NAS carried out food safety inspections across six towns in the Latina province, seizing over 1 t of unsafe food and closing a bar and a fruit shop for serious hygiene violations. Authorities issued EUR 20 000 in fines as part of strict enforcement actions against food safety breaches.

During a hygiene inspection in a butcher shop in the Pedemontana area near Parma, Italian police seized about 1.45 t of expired or untraceable meat with an estimated commercial value of EUR 27 000 and found serious sanitation violations. The production lab attached to the shop was shut down and the owner was fined EUR 4 000. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

The Consumer Protection Authority in Nizwa, shut down an illegal spice-packaging operation and seized over 1 t of adulterated spices lacking proper licensing and labelling. Officials also confiscated packaging equipment and have initiated legal action against those responsible.

Over 3 800 l of oil marketed as “extra virgin olive oil” were seized by Italian authorities near Ravenna after tests showed it was actually coloured seed oil. A couple was charged with commercial fraud in connection with the scheme, which was advertised on social media.

In Islamabad, authorities sealed Pepsi’s main distributor after a raid found expired, fungusinfested sugar with tampered expiry dates and serious hygiene violations, including cockroachcontaminated bags. About 54 874 bags were shut down and production halted.

The Food Safety Authority of Ireland has recalled two grocery products sold in Lidl and Dunnes Stores because of undeclared allergens that could harm people with allergies. One is Dunnes Stores’ Chicken Arrabbiata meal mis-labelled and containing undeclared allergens. The other is Lidl’s Bridge Bakery Oxford Lunch Cake, sold in packs.

In Chatra, authorities uncovered a fake alcoholic beverages operation, arresting six suspects and seizing cartons of counterfeit bottled liquor branded as IMFL during a police raid. The case involves counterfeit production and packaging of spurious alcohol, with fake caps and stickers used to mislead consumers and distribute the product in the open market.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Carabinieri NAS officers in Lecce seized about 2 200 kg of veal, sheep and poultry meat that lacked proper labelling and traceability, posing potential health risks if sold. The company owner was reported to authorities and fined several thousand euros for food safety violations..

The Philippine Navy seized smuggled rice and sugar worth about EUR 1.05 million in maritime operations off Mindanao over three weeks, intercepting three small boats carrying the contraband from Malaysia and Indonesia.. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

Brazil’s Federal Police intercepted a truck containing 22 t of pears and 8 t of shrimp that entered the country without proper documentation, seizing the cargo and arresting the driver for illegal import. The illicit food items lacked legal entry paperwork and were handed over to customs for administrative action, with the suspect detained pending justice.
Indian police arrested two youths in Jetpur (Gujarat) for illegally transporting over 2 200 bottles of alcoholic beverages without valid permits.
About 2 000 kg of subsidised ration rice were seized from a car in Krishnagiri, after the occupants fled during a police check.

In Islamabad, food safety authorities from the Islamabad Food Authority and Punjab Food Authority destroyed 4 000 l of chemically adulterated milk found unfit for consumption and disposed of the harmful additives on the spot. One suspect was arrested and efforts continue to detain the main accused.

In Peshawar, Pakistani food safety authorities raided illegal production sites and seized about 2 000 l of fake cold drinks and 1 000 kg of counterfeit dry yeast from warehouses and manufacturing units. Machinery used to produce and package these unsafe products under well-known brand names was also confiscated.

Peruvian police in the Tacna region seized two trucks and foreign-origin food products suspected of smuggling, detaining both drivers at a rural checkpoint. The confiscated goods and vehicles were valued at about EUR 86 000. Authorities transferred the merchandise to customs storage and handed the suspects over for legal proceedings.
Police in Hung Yen, Vietnam seized nearly 3 t of bean sprouts treated with a banned chemical growth stimulator and charged two producers with violating food safety laws.

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: Police in Ngozi, Burundi, seized 50 kg of dried coffee that was being smuggled towards the border with Rwanda and arrested the suspects.

During a food retail inspection in Les Abymes (Guadeloupe), authorities arrested one individual and seized contraband alcoholic beverages (numerous bottles) and other untaxed products. The operation targeted unregulated sales of undeclared items, posing risks to public health and market integrity. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: Two men were arrested at Aflao, Ghana for allegedly smuggling 14 bags of dried cocoa beans hidden in fertilizer sacks across the Togo border, undermining regulated export controls.

In Bengaluru, authorities seized a large consignment of illegal defence liquor valued at around EUR 24 400 during a crackdown on unauthorised distribution and smuggling operations, disrupting a grey market supply chain for duty-free alcohol.

In Khulna, Bangladesh police seized 697 sacks of illegally stored rice destined for the grey market, arresting one suspect during a raid aimed at curbing illicit food trade and safeguarding regulated supplies.

Italian police in Agrigento uncovered a major olive oil fraud involving 24 suspects accused of mixing low-grade oils with additives to pass it off as extra-virgin olive oil and selling it across Italy and abroad.

The Hawks dismantled a counterfeit liquor syndicate in the Eastern Cape, convicting eight people for running an illegal alcohol-making operation in East London. They were arrested in September 2025 and, in January 2026, the court fined each about EUR 13 000, with suspended prison terms if they reoffend. Investigations into another suspect continue.

Authorities in the Region of Murcia have stepped up checks after discovering that some products labelled and sold as extra-virgin olive oil in shops and supermarkets were not genuine and carried misleading labels, part of an ongoing fraud issue in the sector.

More than 200 kg of seafood and over 4 t of fruit were seized in Licata after police found food being sold without traceability and in poor hygienic-sanitary conditions. Over 20 street vendors were checked, leading to fines exceeding EUR 80 000 and most of the food donated to charity due to safety concerns.

Argentina’s food regulator ANMAT banned the production and sale of a brand of olive oil nationwide, including online, after finding false labelling and non-existent sanitary registrations, classifying it as counterfeit/mislabelled and a potential health risk. Authorities ordered its immediate withdrawal from the market to protect consumers. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

The illegal transportation and seizure of foreign liquor worth about EUR 138 000 occurred in Maharashtra, when excise officials intercepted 1 400 boxes being moved without permits from Goa and arrested one individual.

In Rajasthan, authorities seized over 43 000 l of suspected adulterated ghee during an antiadulteration crackdown. The ghee was found unsafe in laboratory testing, prompting removal from the market and likely legal action.

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: Vietnamese police raided a warehouse in Lam Dong province and seized 4.1 t of fake coffee mixed with soybeans and flavourings meant for the domestic market, amid booming coffee exports..
Police in Belagavi, India seized about 7 000 l of illegally transported alcoholic beverages from Goa valued at around EUR 23 400, after finding it in a truck without valid documentation.

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: In Virudhunagar, authorities uncovered an illegal tea adulteration operation mixing fillers and possibly colourants with tea to deceive buyers, seizing large quantities of impure product and shutting the unit down.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: In Salerno, police raided an illegally operated slaughter site in a filthy apartment and seized about 600 kg of uninspected meat and other foods stored in unsafe conditions, plus another 40 kg from a nearby minimarket, shutting both down.
The Punjab Food Authority in Attock seized 3 200 l of expired cold drinks from a warehouse during a routine inspection and destroyed them to prevent sale.

Police in Ho Chi Minh City uncovered an illegal operation that soaked about 3 000 t of snails in sodium silicate and sold them to markets over five years, risking public health. The processed snails were distributed widely before being seized and the operator charged. January 2026 – JRC Food Fraud Monthly

categories: Cocoa and cocoa preparations, coffee and tea
incidents.description: Vietnamese police have initiated a criminal investigation into a warehouse accused of producing "coffee" from soybeans, seizing 4.1 t of counterfeit coffee products and 3 t of raw materials. The owner admitted to mixing soybeans and flavorings with coffee beans for local market sale.

Bulgarian customs officers seized over 14 t of undeclared vegetables being smuggled from Türkiye to Ukraine hidden among declared fruit shipments. The cargo included cucumbers and tomatoes not supported by documentation, indicating an attempt to bypass customs controls. Authorities imposed an administrative penalty, and the offender paid a fine of EUR 14 000.

A significant seizure of 1 400 l of illegal artisanal liquor was made in Nariño. The operation revealed organized distribution channels supplying informal markets and evading customs controls. Investigations suggest the products entered through unauthorized routes and were redistributed domestically.

A food safety operation identified a company producing unsafe palm candy using banned textile dyes and selling it as baby food, posing serious health risks. Authorities also found counterfeit packaging and unhygienic production conditions. Unsafe products were seized and destroyed. The activity involved multiple food items, including sweets and snack products.

More than 1 000 bottles of wine were seized during an operation targeting illegal commercialization, with products lacking proper documentation and traceability. Authorities identified irregularities suggesting unauthorized distribution and possible misrepresentation of origin. The goods were removed from the market to prevent consumer deception and ensure compliance with regulations. Investigations are ongoing to determine the full extent of the irregular activity February & March 2026 – JRC Food

Authorities intercepted a large-scale food fraud involving tomatoes and onions valued at over EUR 150 000, which were seized before entering the market. The products were reportedly misrepresented regarding origin and documentation to facilitate illegal trade. The operation aimed to protect consumers and ensure compliance with food safety and traceability regulations.

Authorities seized more than 5 t of tomatoes suspected of being smuggled into a wholesale market, lacking proper documentation and traceability. The products were reportedly introduced illegally, bypassing official controls and sanitary requirements.

The Ahmedabad Police seized a large consignment of foreign liquor concealed beneath helmets in a truck, violating Gujarat's prohibition laws. The operation led to the arrest of the truck driver and the confiscation of 10 749 bottles of liquor.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Authorities closed two ethnic restaurants in the Salerno and Piana del Sele areas after inspections revealed serious hygiene deficiencies and lack of traceability for food products.1.4 t of food products were seized and destroyed to protect public health. The establishments failed to comply with EU food safety and documentation requirements.

Customs authorities in Tenkodogo intercepted a fraud operation involving more than 5 000 l of illicit alcohol, preventing its distribution on the market. The seized products were suspected of being unsafe and non-compliant with regulations, posing potential health risks to consumers.

Three individuals were arrested for illegally storing approximately 12 t of subsidized rice intended for public distribution, which was diverted for unauthorized use. Authorities seized the stock and initiated legal action against those involved in the illicit operation.

Authorities in Romania conducted searches in several locations, including Bucharest and nearby counties, targeting companies suspected of importing and distributing fruits from Egypt with pesticide residues above EU limits. Several tonnes of fruit were seized and traced across the supply chain, with warehouses and distribution points inspected.

18 t of olive oil falsely labeled as extra virgin were seized in Salerno, Italy, as part of a joint operation to protect consumers from commercial fraud. The investigation revealed adulteration with lower-grade oils and misleading labeling regarding origin and quality.

Authorities seized five containers of illegally imported fish and animal-based products at Port Klang, valued at EUR 390 000. The goods were suspected of entering without proper certification and inspection, posing potential food safety risks. February & March 2026 – JRC

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Hong Kong Customs seized 4 800 kg of illegally imported food, including frozen meat, and arrested four suspects involved in smuggling activities. The products were imported without required licences and health certificates, violating import regulations. Authorities suspect organised cross-border smuggling using vehicles and a warehouse for storage.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Authorities seized over 12 000 kg of spoiled meat and 7 665 kg of counterfeit cheese during inspections targeting unsafe food practices. The operation aimed to protect public health by removing contaminated and fraudulent products from circulation. Officials highlighted serious hygiene violations and deliberate misrepresentation of food products.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
Poultry meat and poultry meat products
incidents.description: Authorities seized 294 kg of illegal dairy, meat, and plant products at an airport border control point during routine inspections. Most confiscated goods were meat and dairy products carried through passenger and cargo channels, breaching EU import rules.

categories: Meat and meat products (other than poultry)
incidents.description: Authorities at the UK border seized 34 t of illegal meat products, highlighting increasing attempts to smuggle unauthorised animal goods into the country. These products pose serious biosecurity risks, particularly for animal diseases, and were confiscated during intensified inspections. Most items lacked proper documentation or originated from nonapproved sources, indicating illegal trade and misrepresentation.

A Spanish operation uncovered food fraud involving 186 t of frozen fish products that were improperly stored and mislabelled for distribution. Authorities immobilised the products due to traceability issues and potential risks to consumer safety.
